content: Darunavir affects the metabolism of various drugs by influencing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to either increased or decreased drug levels and effects. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Darunavir and Prednisone: Darunavir increases prednisone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, prednisone decreases darunavir levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Darunavir and Primaquine: Darunavir increases primaquine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Darunavir and Primidone: Primidone decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Darunavir and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, Natural): Darunavir increases progesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Darunavir and Propafenone: Darunavir increases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended, especially with antiarrhythmics. 6. Darunavir and Quetiapine: Darunavir increases quetiapine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Darunavir and Quinidine: Darunavir increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin and Darunavir: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Darunavir and Quizartinib: Darunavir increases quizartinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day with strong CYP3A inhibitors and resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 10. Darunavir and Repaglinide: Darunavir increases repaglinide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Rifapentine and Darunavir: Rifapentine decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Darunavir and Rifaximin: Darunavir increases rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Darunavir and Ripretinib: Darunavir increases ripretinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite, DP-5439, raising the risk of adverse reactions. 14. Darunavir and Ritonavir: Darunavir increases ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 15. Darunavir and Rivaroxaban: Darunavir increases rivaroxaban levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Darunavir and Roflumilast (Topical): Darunavir increases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Darunavir and Ropivacaine: Darunavir increases ropivacaine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Darunavir and Rosiglitazone: Darunavir decreases rosiglitazone effects through insulin resistance. Reports of hyperglycemia exist. Use caution and monitor. 19. Darunavir and Rosuvastatin: Darunavir increases rosuvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 20. Rucaparib and Darunavir: Rucaparib increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages if clinically indicated. 21. Rufinamide and Darunavir: Rufinamide decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Darunavir and Saxagliptin: Darunavir increases saxagliptin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Darunavir and Seladelpar: Darunavir increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Darunavir and Sertraline: Darunavir decreases sertraline levels through an unspecified mechanism but also increases sertraline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Dose titration of SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may be required to achieve the desired effect. 25. Darunavir and Sildenafil: Darunavir increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with PDE-5 inhibitors may increase associated adverse reactions such as hypotension, syncope, visual disturbances, and priapism. 26. Darunavir and Sirolimus: Darunavir increases sirolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Darunavir and Sitagliptin: Darunavir decreases sitagliptin effects through insulin resistance. Reports of hyperglycemia exist. Use caution and monitor. 28. Darunavir and Solifenacin: Darunavir increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Darunavir and Sorafenib: Darunavir increases sorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Darunavir and Stiripentol: Darunavir increases stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Stiripentol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects. 31. Darunavir and Sufentanil SL: Darunavir increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 32. Darunavir and Sunitinib: Darunavir increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Darunavir and Tacrolimus (Oral and Ointment): Darunavir increases tacrolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 34. Darunavir and Tasimelteon: Darunavir increases tasimelteon levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Tazemetostat and Darunavir: Tazemetostat decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Tecovirimat and Darunavir: Tecovirimat decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 37. Darunavir and Temsirolimus: Darunavir increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Darunavir and Teniposide: Darunavir increases teniposide levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Darunavir and Terbinafine: Darunavir increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Darunavir and Tezacaftor: Darunavir increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 41. Darunavir and Theophylline: Darunavir increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Darunavir and Tiagabine: Darunavir increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Darunavir and Tinidazole: Darunavir increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Darunavir and Tipranavir: Darunavir increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 45. Darunavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Darunavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects due to increased systemic exposure to its active metabolite (MMAE). 46. Darunavir and Tolterodine: Darunavir increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Topiramate and Darunavir: Topiramate decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Darunavir and Toremifene: Darunavir increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential inhibition of toremifene metabolism. 49. Darunavir and Tramadol: Darunavir increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. A reduced tramadol dose may be required. 50. Darunavir and Trazodone: Darunavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose titration of antidepressants may be required to achieve the desired effect. 51. Darunavir and Triamcinolone Acetonide (Injectable Suspension): Darunavir increases triamcinolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 52. Darunavir and Trimipramine: Darunavir increases trimipramine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Ublituximab and Darunavir: Ublituximab decreases darunavir effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 54. Darunavir and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol (Inhaled): Darunavir increases umeclidinium and vilanterol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 55. Darunavir and Upadacitinib: Darunavir increases upadacitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor, especially with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Darunavir and Valbenazine: Darunavir increases valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 57. Darunavir and Vamorolone: Darunavir increases vamorolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 58. Darunavir and Vardenafil: Darunavir increases vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 59. Darunavir and Verapamil: Darunavir increases verapamil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 60. Darunavir and Vilanterol/Fluticasone Furoate (Inhaled): Darunavir increases vilanterol and fluticasone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 61. Darunavir and Vinblastine: Darunavir increases vinblastine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects. Consider withholding antiretroviral therapy if significant side effects occur. 62. Darunavir and Vincristine: Darunavir increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects. Consider withholding antiretroviral therapy if significant side effects occur. 63. Voriconazole and Darunavir: Voriconazole increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 64. Darunavir and Vortioxetine: Darunavir increases vortioxetine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Darunavir and Warfarin: Warfarin serum concentrations may increase or decrease. Darunavir may increase levels of the less potent R-enantiomer of warfarin, but ritonavir co-administration may decrease R-warfarin levels. Use caution and monitor. 66. Zafirlukast and Darunavir: Zafirlukast increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 67. Darunavir and Zanubrutinib: Darunavir increases zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor.
